new_candidates.duration: 183 days from the ordinance's effective date; because the vote was not unanimous, the ordinance takes effect 30 days after passage (approximately 2026-08-13)
new_candidates.legal_basis: City of Jackson ordinance adopted by City Council 5-2 on July 14, 2026, establishing a citywide data center application moratorium
new_candidates.trigger: Council sought time to identify appropriate sites, study impacts, and develop a data center regulatory framework
new_candidates.current_status: Adopted July 14, 2026 by a 5-2 council vote; no further council vote is required for it to take effect. Because the vote was not unanimous, the ordinance does not take legal effect until 30 days after passage (approximately August 13, 2026), then runs 183 days from that effective date. As of the July 31, 2026 research date the ordinance had passed council but had not yet reached its effective date. During the moratorium the city will not accept, process, or approve data center applications for special or conditional use permits, zoning map amendments, building permits, or other zoning changes. Approximately 1,100 acres of city-owned land around Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport are exempted.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Citywide; no single named project. Excludes approximately 1,100 acres of city-owned land near Jackson-Medgar Wiley Evers International Airport.
new_candidates.outcome: Enacted by council vote; scheduled to take legal effect approximately 30 days after passage.

new_candidates.notes: A standalone signed or codified ordinance file was not located on the city website as of July 31, 2026; sourced from the official agenda, archived council video, and two contemporaneous news reports. A prior 6-month proposal was tabled 4-2 by the same council on May 19, 2026 after a notice-timing objection from city attorneys (the item had been noticed on May 5, one day short of the 15-day requirement); that tabled version is excluded here under the failed/tabled proposal rule and is not the same instrument as the enacted July 14 ordinance.
